members.name: var_a
members.instructions: Classify this tweet under a hate-speech annotation policy that covers only hate against women and hate against immigrants/refugees. Judge what the tweet's own words do, and who the target is. Pick the option that best describes the tweet.

criteria.misogynistic_attack: An angry, degrading attack on a woman or girl, women as a group, or a person who is not a man: insulting, threatening or sexually objectifying her/them, e.g. 'shut your bitch ass up, your hoe ass...', 'fucking whore', saying women are inferior or deserve harm. Real hostility toward the target is required. Also hate: putting someone down by saying what they are, 'you are (such) a bitch/hoe' ('why r u such a bitch') — not 'bitch' or 'hoe' used as a filler or form of address in ordinary talk ('bitch I ain't got that money', 'turn your map on bitch'), and degrading generalisations about women as hoes or bitches ('I don't follow hoes who are just cute'). Threatening violence against someone called a bitch or hoe ('you can get dragged bitch real quick') is also hate. Telling someone (not a man) to shut up while calling them a whore ('bitch shut the fuck up... ur fuckin whore') is hate.
criteria.slur_at_male_or_unclear_target: A slur such as bitch, hoe, whore, cunt or son of a bitch used to insult a man (e.g. a male politician), men, or an unknown person in a mild way (e.g. 'whoever unfollowed me, you a bitch'). Not about women. A man is the target when the tweet says so (e.g. 'this dude... shut up little bitch'). The same goes for slurs aimed at a general or unknown audience ('anyone who doubted Louis is just a bitter bitch').
criteria.casual_or_self_slang: Words like bitch or hoe used casually: addressing someone in a question, joke, banter or mild annoyance ('are those not grapes bitch?', 'you can't expose me on my birthday hoe'), affectionately to a friend, about oneself, as an exclamation or stream of swearing, about a situation, or the author complaining about being called such names. 'Bitch' or 'hoe' as a filler word or form of address ('bitch I ain't got that kinda money', 'okay bitch tf... whore 😜') belongs here. Karma remarks ('karma's a bitch hoe, you gon get yours') belong here.
criteria.immigrant_attack: The tweet's text says something negative about immigrants, refugees, migrants or 'illegals' themselves: insults or dehumanises them (scum, pigs, savages, rapefugees), calls their arrival an invasion, presents them as criminals, rapists, diseased or a welfare burden (including news of a crime by an illegal immigrant), or itself says they should be deported or sent home. Also counts: a bare exclamation with no political target ('Well stated!', 'Can't be real!?') whose whole message is #DeportThemAll. Using a slur for refugees such as 'rapefugee', even in passing, also counts. Saying illegal immigrants are cheap labour that politicians protect over citizens, with #SendThemBack-type hashtags, also counts. The text itself calling immigration an invasion, even in passing ('walls are a valid response to an invasion'), or saying the country is being given away and cannot sustain them, also counts.
criteria.immigration_politics: Tweets whose text is about a politician, president, party, Congress or court and what they do (thanks, pleas, advice, criticism, insults), even when they end with #DeportThemAll, #DeportAllOfThem, #BuildTheWall or #SendThemBack — but not when the text mocks or belittles the immigrants themselves (e.g. '@NancyPelosi and her precious illegal aliens! #DeportThemAll' is an attack). The text is about politicians, Democrats/liberals, the media, Twitter, elections, rallies, wall funding or ICE policy (including insults aimed at politicians or liberals), or is a bare slogan or joke with a hashtag, or just uses the term 'illegal aliens', and says nothing negative about immigrants themselves. Slogan hashtags such as #BuildTheWall, #SendThemBack or #SendThemHome do not by themselves make a tweet hateful: an insult at a politician, a neutral news headline about migration, or a vague remark followed by such hashtags is not hateful. Explaining or defending the term 'illegal alien' ('they are here illegally and alien to our soil, hence the term') is not an attack. A vague remark followed by a slogan hashtag ('Australia needs to do nothing of the sort. #sendthemback') is not an attack. A tweet about the media, politicians or election seats that only adds #StopTheInvasion-type hashtags ('the more they lie, the less people listen to MSM #StopTheInvasion', 'Illegals give blue states 20 congressional seats') is not an attack.
criteria.other: Anything else, not hateful toward women or immigrants.

misogynistic_attack.definition: Real, degrading hostility aimed at a woman, women, or a person who is not a man.
includes: angry slur attacks such as 'shut your bitch ass up, your hoe ass' or 'fucking whore'
threats or sexual objectification of women
saying women are inferior or deserve harm

putting someone down by saying what they are, 'you are (such) a bitch/hoe' ('why r u such a bitch') — not 'bitch' or 'hoe' used as a filler or form of address in ordinary talk ('bitch I ain't got that money', 'turn your map on bitch')
degrading generalisations about women as hoes or bitches ('I don't follow hoes who are just cute')
threatening violence against someone called a bitch or hoe ('you can get dragged bitch real quick')
telling someone (not a man) to shut up while calling them a whore ('bitch shut the fuck up... ur fuckin whore')

slur_at_male_or_unclear_target.definition: A gendered slur (bitch, hoe, whore, cunt, son of a bitch) aimed at a man, men, or an unknown person in a mild way.
examples: a male senator called a whore
'this dude... shut the hell up little bitch'
'anyone who doubted Louis is just a bitter bitch' (a general or unknown audience)

casual_or_self_slang.definition: bitch/hoe as everyday slang without real hostility.

affection between friends
talking about oneself
exclamations or swearing streams
complaining about being called names
bitch/hoe/whore as a filler word or form of address ('bitch I ain't got that kinda money', 'okay bitch tf... whore 😜')
karma remarks ('karma's a bitch hoe, you gon get yours')

immigrant_attack.definition: Negative claims about immigrants, refugees, migrants or illegals as people, or wanting them removed.
includes: insults or dehumanising terms (scum, pigs, savages, rapefugees)
invasion talk
portraying them as criminals, rapists, diseased or welfare burdens, including crime reports about illegal immigrants
saying they should be deported, sent home or got out
a bare exclamation with no political target ('Well stated!', 'Can't be real!?') whose whole message is #DeportThemAll
using a slur for refugees such as 'rapefugee', even in passing
saying illegal immigrants are cheap labour that politicians protect over citizens, with #SendThemBack-type hashtags
the text itself calling immigration an invasion, even in passing ('walls are a valid response to an invasion')
saying the country is being given away or cannot sustain them ('we are giving our country away, we cannot sustain this')

immigration_politics.definition: Tweets whose text is about a politician, president, party, Congress or court and what they do (thanks, pleas, advice, criticism, insults), even when they end with #DeportThemAll, #DeportAllOfThem, #BuildTheWall or #SendThemBack — but not when the text mocks or belittles the immigrants themselves (e.g. '@NancyPelosi and her precious illegal aliens! #DeportThemAll' is an attack). a bare slogan or joke with a hashtag
merely using the term 'illegal aliens'
explaining or defending the term 'illegal alien' ('they are here illegally and alien to our soil, hence the term')

a tweet about the media, politicians or election seats that only adds #StopTheInvasion-type hashtags ('the more they lie, the less people listen to MSM #StopTheInvasion', 'Illegals give blue states 20 congressional seats')
immigration_politics.note: Slogan hashtags such as #BuildTheWall, #SendThemBack or #SendThemHome do not by themselves make a tweet hateful: an insult at a politician, a neutral news headline about migration, or a vague remark followed by such hashtags is not hateful.
